title: Stakeholder coverage and RACI
objective: Identify the gap in an interview containing only the AE and an IT administrator.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Blueprint conclusions are only as good as the people who informed them. You need business sponsorship, functional leadership, front-line workflow knowledge, and technical or data ownership. Security and compliance join when they are relevant.

head: Stakeholder

blocks.x: For each person, record which of four things they hold: a **decision**, an **input**, a **metric**, or a **dependency**. Invite the right voices to each meeting, not everyone to every meeting. A DITL session with ten observers and one user produces less evidence than a session with two users and a note-taker.

blocks.label: Watch for
blocks.x: Mistaking seniority for workflow expertise. A director can describe the target state, but often only the people doing the work can describe today's friction accurately. Respect recording, privacy, and access constraints when notes are shared between organizations.
Who to interview depends on the account

Glean's DITL training notes that the right interviewee shifts with account size. In corporate and commercial accounts, the person one level below the VP often understands the workflow well enough to walk through it step by step. In enterprise and strategic accounts, you usually need the people who do the work every day, the employees whose work would actually change.
Either way, ask the question directly: "Who touches this workflow, and who would be using the new process?"

blocks.title: Stakeholder coverage by influence and workflow knowledge
blocks.alt: A two-by-two matrix with workflow knowledge on the horizontal axis and decision influence on the vertical axis. High influence and high knowledge: business owners, who define impact. High influence and low knowledge: the executive sponsor, who makes the decision. Low influence and high knowledge: front-line users, who explain the real work. Low influence and low knowledge: inform as needed.
